description: Satellite imagery captured by the Spot 5 sensor, displaying a landscape composed of vegetated and bare rock areas in a Near-Infrared (NIR), Red (R), Green (G) false-colour band combination. The image has a spatial resolution of 2.5 m. Dense vegetation appears in bright red, indicating high chlorophyll activity, while other vegetated areas appear in greenish-blue. A winding, lighter blue-green feature on the left may represent a bare path or a dry stream bed. A yellow vector line delineates a land cover polygon in the lower central part of the image, encompassing areas of both red vegetation and lighter, possibly bare, patches. The numerical label "9990" is visible within this delineated polygon. A second yellow line crosses the upper portion of the image. The image illustrates "Bare rocks formations" (CLMS category 6.3.1.1) which typically feature less than 10% high vegetation cover. The acquisition date is partially visible as "Date: 2[unreadable]".
